description: The count and the average cover every playlist in `Playlist`, and playlists with no track entries count as zero.

d.request: Return the 10 playlists with the highest ratio of track count to the average track count across all playlists in `Playlist`, counting playlists with no `PlaylistTrack` entries as zero; show each playlist’s ID, track count, and unrounded ratio, sorted by ratio descending with missing ratios last.
d.sql: WITH playlist_counts AS (SELECT p.PlaylistId, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM Playlist AS p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack AS pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId GROUP BY p.PlaylistId), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(track_count) AS avg_track_count FROM playlist_counts) SELECT pc.PlaylistId, pc.track_count, 1.0 * pc.track_count / NULLIF(ac.avg_track_count, 0) AS ratio FROM playlist_counts AS pc CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC, pc.PlaylistId LIMIT 10;

c.request: What are the 10 playlists with the most tracks relative to the average number of tracks per playlist? For each one, show the playlist id, its track count and the ratio of that count to the average (unrounded). Sort by the ratio from highest to lowest, with any missing ratios last. The count and the average cover every playlist in `Playlist`, and playlists with no track entries count as zero.
c.sql: WITH playlist_counts AS (SELECT p.PlaylistId, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM Playlist AS p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack AS pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId GROUP BY p.PlaylistId), ratios AS (SELECT PlaylistId, track_count, CAST(track_count AS REAL) / NULLIF((SELECT AVG(track_count) FROM playlist_counts), 0) AS ratio FROM playlist_counts) SELECT PlaylistId, track_count, ratio FROM ratios ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC, PlaylistId LIMIT 10;

a.request: Considering every playlist in `Playlist`, including those with no entries in `PlaylistTrack` (which count as zero), count each playlist's track entries and work out the average of these counts across all of these playlists. For the 10 playlists with the highest ratio of track count to that average, show the playlist id, its track count and the ratio (count ÷ average, unrounded), sorted by the ratio from highest to lowest with any missing ratios last.
a.sql: WITH playlist_counts AS (SELECT p.PlaylistId, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM Playlist AS p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack AS pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId GROUP BY p.PlaylistId), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(track_count) AS avg_count FROM playlist_counts), ratios AS (SELECT pc.PlaylistId, pc.track_count, pc.track_count / NULLIF(ac.avg_count, 0) AS ratio FROM playlist_counts AS pc CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac) SELECT PlaylistId, track_count, ratio FROM ratios ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Return the 10 playlists with the highest track count divided by the average track count across all playlists in `Playlist`, including playlists with no `PlaylistTrack` entries as zero; show each playlist’s ID, track count, and unrounded ratio, ordered by ratio descending with missing ratios last.
b.sql: WITH playlist_counts AS (SELECT p.PlaylistId, COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM Playlist AS p LEFT JOIN PlaylistTrack AS pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId GROUP BY p.PlaylistId), playlist_ratios AS (SELECT PlaylistId, track_count, CAST(track_count AS REAL) / NULLIF((SELECT AVG(track_count) FROM playlist_counts), 0) AS ratio FROM playlist_counts) SELECT PlaylistId, track_count, ratio FROM playlist_ratios ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC, PlaylistId LIMIT 10;
